Job Description The Safety Officer is a full-time, on-site role based in the Maldives. The worksite is the Fuel Terminal at Funadhoo Island located near Malé City, Maldives. Job Responsibilities Operate the Permit to Work system covering hot work, confined space entry, working at height, excavation, line breaking and underwater work at the jetty. Enforce gas testing, isolation and lock-out/tag-out, and hazardous area (Zone 0/1/2) compliance around gasoline tanks, vapor spaces, pump rooms and loading gantries. Control static electricity, bonding and earthing, and vapor ignition risks during gasoline receipt, loading and tank cleaning Conduct daily field inspections of tank farm, bunds, manifolds, pump house, gantry and jetty; log unsafe acts and conditions and drive them to closure and conduct JHA and JSA. Manage contractor HSE performance: induction, method statement review, toolbox talks and field supervision. Jetty and Marine Transfer Verify ship/shore safety checklist completion and the pre-transfer meeting for every tanker discharge. Inspect hoses, quick-release couplings, emergency shutdown systems and mooring arrangements, witness pressure testing and certification. Enforce jetty controls: no smoking and no naked light zones, hot work embargo during transfer, safe access, life-saving appliance readiness and personal flotation devices for work over water Ensure oil spill containment equipment (booms, skimmers, sorbents, approved dispersants) is inspected, and ready before every transfer. Coordinate with vessel masters, the port and harbor authority, and the MNDF Coast Guard on transfer safety and incident notification. Environmental Compliance Ensure compliance with Maldives EPA requirements, MARPOL Annex I and the terminal’s environmental permits Maintain the Oil Spill Contingency Plan and Tier 1 response capability; verify bund integrity, interceptors and oily water discharge monitoring. Manage hazardous and general waste handling, sludge disposal and environmental record keeping. Emergency Preparedness Maintain inspection and test schedules for foam systems, deluge, hydrants, monitors, extinguishers and flammable gas and flame detection. Plan and run drills covering tank fire, gasoline spill, jetty and vessel emergency, ESD activation, medical evacuation and site evacuation; document lessons learned. Maintain the Emergency Response Plan and liaison with MNDF Fire and Rescue, Coast Guard, port authority and neighboring island stakeholders Compliance, Investigation and Reporting Ensure compliance with Maldivian occupational safety, fire and environmental regulations, port rules, ISPS Code security requirements and company standards Investigate incidents, near misses and spills to root cause; issue reports and track corrective actions to closure Compile monthly HSE statistics (LTI, TRIR, near-miss reporting rate, audit closure) for management review Training and Safety Culture Deliver HSE induction and refresher training for staff, contractors, tanker drivers and boat crew Lead the terminal HSE function and drive near-miss and behavioral safety reporting Required Qualifications NEBOSH IGC OR Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical/Chemical/Process Engineering Preferred Requirements Excellent knowledge of potentially hazardous materials or practices Proficiency in MS Office Working knowledge of safety management information system and PTW systems Great interpersonal and communication skills Fluent written and spoken English; Dhivehi a strong advantage ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 internal auditor certification IOSH Managing Safely OSRL or equivalent Tier 1 oil spill response training Prior marine and port experience Familiarity with ISGOTT and ISPS code requirements Salary and Benefits Salary Negotiable  Health insurance will be provided after probation Staff Privilege Program How to Apply Apply via LinkedIn

review_candidates.title: Research Analyst (Global Partnerships)
review_candidates.description: About Gate Founded in 2013, Gate is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges. We operate remote-first across multiple time zones, with a culture built around ownership, speed and direct communication. Why This Role Exists Gate’s Global Partnerships team works across three broad areas: CEX asset listings Web3 and Earn product partnerships, including DeFi, DEX, wallets and blockchain infrastructure TradFi and tokenised-finance partnerships, including brokers, market makers, liquidity providers, stablecoins and RWAs As the range of opportunities grows, we need someone who can help the team decide what is worth pursuing, how it should be structured and how to make those decisions consistently. This is not a pure desk-research role, and it is not limited to asset listings. You will stay close to fast-moving crypto markets, pressure-test companies and opportunities, compare commercial terms, and turn scattered information into a clear recommendation. You will also help build the frameworks, SOPs and internal systems that make the entire partnerships team more effective. You will work closely with senior partnerships leads and receive active mentoring, but you will still be expected to take ownership of your work and develop an independent point of view. What You’ll Own Track market developments, competitor activity and emerging opportunities across CEX listings, Web3/Earn products and TradFi partnerships Translate management direction into category strategies, market maps and actionable priorities, including where Gate should enter, follow, differentiate or pass Evaluate prospective assets and partners across team quality, investors, product, adoption, token or business economics, market and on-chain data, reputation and key risks Follow relevant projects and ecosystems closely enough to identify important shifts early—not only after they become obvious from public headlines Research comparable partnerships and benchmark commercial structures, including pricing, fees, revenue sharing, incentives, liquidity commitments and other key terms Turn research into a concise recommendation: pursue, deprioritise or pass; why; the proposed approach; and the next action required Help design and maintain opportunity-assessment frameworks, decision criteria, scoring models and pipeline-prioritisation methods Build and improve SOPs and templates covering opportunity intake, due diligence, internal approvals, handover, execution tracking and post-deal review Maintain structured internal knowledge covering partner profiles, competitor activity, comparable terms, previous decisions and lessons from completed deals Support partnership strategy, negotiation preparation and concise updates for the team and senior management Review the results of past decisions and use what happened afterwards to improve the team’s frameworks and judgment over time Who We’re Looking For Typically 2–4 years of experience in strategy, consulting, investment banking, venture capital or digital-asset research. Exceptional earlier-career candidates will also be considered Fluent English communication with strong commercial writing ability. Strong Chinese proficiency is a major asset Strong analytical and commercial judgment—you can form a view, explain the reasoning and recommend what should happen next, rather than simply summarising information Genuine hands-on interest in crypto markets. You follow projects and market activity closely and can speak credibly about recent developments across CEX, on-chain, DeFi, DEX, wallets or Earn products Structured thinking and an interest in turning messy work into clear frameworks, SOPs and repeatable processes. Prior experience doing this is useful, but we are also open to someone who can grow into it with mentoring Comfortable comparing commercial terms and understanding the incentives of different parties in a deal Curious and adaptable enough to work across both crypto-native and TradFi opportunities rather than staying within one narrow sector Able to manage several workstreams, move quickly and take ownership in a remote-first environment Nice to Have Experience with an exchange, trading platform, fund, research firm, fintech company or fast-moving crypto product team Exposure to asset listings, brokers, market makers, stablecoins, tokenisation, RWAs, DeFi, wallets, Earn products or blockchain infrastructure Experience building dashboards, databases, research tools or lightweight automations, including effective use of AI tools to accelerate analysis Experience analysing partnership economics, transaction structures or comparable commercial terms Why This Role Is Worth Your Time Your work will feed directly into live partnership decisions across crypto and traditional finance. You will not just produce reports—you will help decide which opportunities Gate pursues, how deals are structured and how the team operates. For someone earlier in their career, this is a chance to get unusually broad exposure to listings, Web3 products and TradFi partnerships while working closely with experienced deal leads. You will build a visible track record of decisions, frameworks and commercial outcomes, with room to take on substantially more ownership as you grow.

review_candidates.title: Regional Operations Lead (Southeast Asia)
review_candidates.description: Regional Operations Lead - Southeast Asia | Based in Malaysia Lead the region. Strengthen teams. Build trusted client relationships. Improve patient access. Axios International is seeking a strong, hands-on Regional Operations Lead to lead programmes, people and client relationships across Southeast Asia. Reporting to the Global Operations Lead. Based in Malaysia, the role will initially cover Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines, with India or other markets potentially added as the regional scope evolves. This is not a traditional coordination role. We are looking for an experienced regional leader who can create clarity and accountability, develop local managers, represent Axios credibly with pharmaceutical clients, and ensure that regional teams receive the decisions, expertise and support they need to succeed. The Role Provide visible and accessible leadership to country, programme and operational teams across the region. Lead complex Patient Assistance Programs, Patient Support Programs and other patient-access services, ensuring high-quality, compliant and patient-centred delivery. Set priorities, clarify responsibilities, coach managers and build a culture of ownership, collaboration and accountability. Act as the senior regional contact for key pharmaceutical clients and stakeholders, building trust and leading the resolution of significant programme or relationship issues. Represent the needs of the region within Axios, secure timely operational and functional support, and escalate unresolved matters constructively through the appropriate leadership channels. Oversee regional performance, capacity, programme revenues, P&L, cost centres, operational risks and improvement actions. Identify opportunities to retain, strengthen and expand client relationships and work with Business Excellence and commercial colleagues to shape credible new opportunities. Maintain direct exposure to field realities through regular regional travel and engagement with teams, clients, healthcare professionals, institutions and partners. What We Are Looking For Substantial experience in healthcare, pharmaceuticals, patient assistance, patient support or patient-access services. Proven leadership of teams and managers across multiple countries, business units or complex stakeholder environments. Strong senior client-facing capability, with the confidence to manage difficult discussions and build long-term relationships. The judgement and presence to challenge constructively, advocate for regional priorities and secure action from senior and global stakeholders. A strong operational track record, including programme performance, budgets, resources, risk, quality and compliance. An ability to remain close to operational realities while leading through managers rather than becoming the solution to every issue. Excellent written and spoken English and the flexibility to travel regularly across the assigned region. We Would Particularly Value Experience in Southeast Asian healthcare markets, particularly Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines. Experience in India or another complex, culturally diverse regional market. Knowledge of market access and the design or delivery of Patient Assistance Programs and Patient Support Programs. Experience working in a matrixed international organization and obtaining support from global functions. An established professional network within the pharmaceutical or healthcare sector and relevant regional language capability. The Leadership Profile The Successful Candidate Will Combine The ability to bring people together, delegate effectively and create clear accountability. The drive to challenge obstacles, make timely decisions and follow issues through to resolution. The relationship-building capability to engage clients, partners and internal stakeholders with credibility. The discipline to turn priorities and decisions into consistent execution across countries and programmes. Why this role matters Behind every operational challenge may be a patient waiting for access to treatment. This role offers the opportunity to strengthen regional leadership, develop capable teams, build trusted client partnerships and help ensure that programmes deliver reliable support to patients across Southeast Asia. How To Apply Please submit your CV together with a concise cover note specifically explaining your experience leading multi-country healthcare operations, developing teams and managing senior pharmaceutical clients.
